name: Oswald Mosley
period: British Union of Fascists leadership, 1932–1940; post-war European programme excluded
role: Leader of the British Union of Fascists
description: British fascist leader assessed during the BUF period, including corporatist economic proposals, imperial trade and opposition to war with Germany.

religion.reason: Political references to Christian service do not firmly establish personal religious identification during BUF leadership.

sources.title: Mosley announces programme for new fascist party

axes.brief: A corporative fascist executive would replace conventional competitive parliamentary government.
axes.counterEvidence: Early parliamentary service and occupational voting proposals do not establish universal equal control of the executive.

axes.brief: Political discipline and suppression of opposition are more consistent with the proposed fascist state.
axes.counterEvidence: His own later internment and claimed free-expression rights are counter-evidence; nationalist censorship is not viewpoint-neutral hate-speech law.

axes.brief: Imperial British identity and later BUF antisemitism restrict equal cultural plurality.
axes.counterEvidence: Initial denials of anti-Jewish intent must be recorded alongside subsequent agitation; the later Europe-a-Nation programme is out of scope.

qualifications.15: The statement specifically includes several distinct ways of life within national identity; it does not ask whether a common national identity should exist.

axes.brief: National preference and exclusion of perceived outsiders favour restricted settlement.
axes.counterEvidence: Economic integration within the Empire differs from general non-imperial immigration.

qualifications.5: The statement permits permanent refugee settlement regardless of skills or cultural compatibility. The answer concerns this unconditional clause, separately from selected humanitarian admissions.

axes.brief: Imperial defence coexists with opposition to British war against Germany.
axes.counterEvidence: Anti-war campaigning in that conflict does not establish general pacifism; BUF paramilitary violence remains relevant counter-evidence.

axes.brief: Imperial economic and political sovereignty constrain foreign jurisdiction.
axes.counterEvidence: Post-war European federation cannot be backdated into the 1932–1940 imperial programme.

axes.brief: Private firms operate within corporative national direction and strategic public services.
axes.counterEvidence: A state economic framework is not universal state ownership; the primary summary describes private firms and profit sharing.

axes.brief: A protected Empire-wide economic bloc would replace dependence on outside markets.
axes.counterEvidence: Trade within the imperial bloc remains encouraged; protection is geographically selective.

axes.brief: Corporative coordination and national production priorities override unregulated market allocation.
axes.counterEvidence: Private enterprise remains, so this is coordinated corporatism rather than a fully specified socialist command economy.

axes.brief: Worker purchasing power and social provision are part of the national economic programme.
axes.counterEvidence: Property and hierarchical corporative institutions limit equalisation; no comprehensive modern wealth-tax schedule is documented.

axes.brief: Christian cultural language coexists with a political state not clearly assigned to clerical control.
axes.counterEvidence: Christian service rhetoric does not imply religious courts or personal Christian eligibility.

axes.brief: National hierarchy and conventional family ideals favour traditional social institutions.
axes.counterEvidence: Women’s party participation complicates a claim that every public role was restricted to men.

axes.brief: Modern industrial capacity and technical organisation are important to the BUF programme.
axes.counterEvidence: Technocratic production does not establish unrestricted biomedical experimentation or indifference to heritage.

axes.brief: A strong national corporative executive limits independent regional political authority.
axes.counterEvidence: Occupational representation and local administration are not autonomous federal sovereignty.

axes.brief: Fascist character formation coexists with exclusionary national and conventional sex-role assumptions.
axes.counterEvidence: Antisemitism does not establish a detailed biological theory for every intelligence or behavioural question.
